claim: Let \(G\) be a finite connected simple graph with \(n\) vertices, \(m\) edges, minimum degree at least \(2\), and girth at least \(5\). Then the Lovász neighborhood complex \(\mathcal N(G)\) simplicially collapses to a graph. If \(G\) is non-bipartite, then \(\mathcal N(G)\simeq \bigvee^{2m-2n+1}S^1\). If \(G\) is bipartite, then \(\mathcal N(G)\) has exactly two connected components and each is homotopy equivalent to \(\bigvee^{m-n+1}S^1\).
integrity: The proof is all-parameter. Finite computations in verify.py only corroborate the explicit collapse mechanism on representative regular, irregular, bipartite, and non-bipartite examples.
scientific_limitations: The theorem requires a finite connected simple graph, minimum degree at least 2, and girth at least 5. No extension to triangles, quadrangles, leaves, or closed-neighborhood complexes is claimed.
title: High-girth neighborhood complexes collapse to explicit graph wedges
